findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared between controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single mutable array on the class prototype, so every CreateAccountController instance (and any re-instantiation of the modal) shares the same array. Emails rejected in one session/modal will keep being flagged as invalid afterwards, and the list is never reset. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in `init`, or via a computed/`Em.A()` created on first use).

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw submitted email. Emails stored in the table with different casing (or a user signing up with `Bad@Spamclub.com` when `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked) will not match, so the block is trivially bypassed. Normalize with `Email.downcase` on both write (before_validation) and lookup.

findings.title: match_count increment is non-atomic and written inside a validation
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` performs a read-modify-write, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose increments. Worse, this write happens from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, i.e. inside the enclosing `User` save transaction; if that transaction rolls back the statistics update is discarded. Use `update_all`/`increment_counter` outside the caller's transaction.

findings.title: Validator performs a DB write on every email validation, including valid?/preview calls
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates and saves the matched row. Since `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` runs on every `valid?` call (e.g. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` before `user.save`), match_count can be incremented multiple times per signup attempt, making the statistic unreliable.

findings.title: Signup failure response now echoes submitted attributes without restricting fields
findings.body: `user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` plus `user.errors.to_hash` are returned in the failure JSON. This is fine for the three listed fields, but note the response now exposes the raw internal error keys; if more attributes are ever added to the slice (or the model gains sensitive attributes) they would leak to an unauthenticated endpoint. Consider returning only the explicitly needed values and documenting the contract, since the JS only uses `result.values.email`.

findings.title: No tests for whitelist/blacklist paths moved into the new validator
findings.body: The whitelist/blacklist logic was deleted from `User#email_validator` and moved to `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email branch. Any regression in the domain whitelist/blacklist behaviour (including the interaction where a whitelist/blacklist error suppresses the blocked check) would go undetected unless equivalent specs were moved too.
